page.layout: One page of running text in one column. At the top: running head "LIBER I." centred, page number "13" at the top right. Below it: a chapter heading (ARTICULUS VI. with its subtitle), then the body text in paragraphs. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: ARTICULUS VI.
CUm agimus de atomis, censemus eas à Deo
creatas, quod fuit præmonendum. Plato in Ti-
mæo de illis primis corporibus, Igne scilicet, Aere,
Aqua, & Terra loquitur hunc in modum: De his

l.i: omnibus adeo parvis ita putandum est, quod si singula
duntaxat singulorum generum capiantur, nullum eo-
rum propter parvitatem cerni à nobis poterit, sin multa

main_text.l: que cernentur. Hæc Plato. Quapropter craffius illi
de hac subtilitate cogitant, qui has Democriti Ato-
mos putant similes illis minutis quæ loco opaco per
transversos Solis radios volitare conspiciuntur; cum
in singulis illis corpusculis, vel mille, quales agnovit
Democritus atomos agnoscere queas; si, quod ab ex-
perientia ratio clarissimum facit, consideres.
Pediculi illi intercutes, quos cirones vulgo vo-
cant, cum sint tantæ tenuitatis, ut aciculæ cuspide
admotos ad lucem vix capiat visus acutissimus; ani-
malia sunt sensu communicantia; neque enim tan-
tum nutriuntur & crescunt, quod animæ vegetantis
beneficio tribuitur: sed suffossione facta, quasi cuni-
culis incedunt, magna cum mutatione & sensione
partis. Est igitur anima sentiens, & quidem in cor-
pore organico, atque adeo ex plurimis organis con-
structo, quorum singula quam multis partibus con-
stant, fidem excedit. Nisi forte quis adeo fuerit

l.i: imperitus, ut putet eam nutritionem, attractionem
fieri; vel incessum sine vi; vel vim illam sine organis
cieri; quæ & cutem transforent [?], & papulam cum
pruritu excitent, & aquam veluti nutritionis excre-

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. Doubtful reading: "transforent" (possibly transfodient), marked [?]. Long s rendered as s throughout. The word "Atomos" and other line-end hyphens (Ti-, Ato-, eo-, ex-, con-, du-) are kept as printed. The paragraph ends mid-word at "du-" and continues on the next page. The stray marks at the left of the running head and at the margins are not printed text and are left out.
